hints: Notice particle X is at zero displacement on the displacement-distance graph at $t=0$, on the rising section just after a trough and before the peak at $\lambda$.
For a wave travelling to the right, the displacement at fixed X becomes what was previously just to the left of X, where the rope is at negative displacement.
So the displacement-time graph for X must start at $0$ and go negative first, then oscillate with period $T$.
walkthrough: Read the displacement-distance snapshot at $t=0$: particle X has displacement $0$ and lies on a slope that rises to the right toward the next crest near $\lambda$.

Recall the rule for a travelling profile: with direction of travel to the right, the whole shape shifts right with speed $v = \lambda / T$, so the new displacement at X equals the old displacement just to the left of X.
Just to the left of X the displacement is negative because that point is on the side of the trough, so X must next move downward to negative displacement.
Therefore the displacement-time graph must start at $0$ at $t=0$, go negative first, pass through zero at $T/2$, reach a positive peak, and return to zero at $T$.
Only the graph that starts at zero, goes to a trough then a crest over one period $T$ matches this motion. This is option C.

A.explanation: This starts at zero and moves to positive displacement, which would require the trough to the left of X to move away. The wave moving to the right brings negative displacement to X.

B.explanation: This starts at maximum positive displacement with period $T$. Particle X starts at zero displacement at $t=0$, not at a crest.

C.explanation: Particle X starts at zero and the rightward-moving profile brings the negative displacement from just to its left to X, so it moves negative first and repeats with period $T$.

D.explanation: This starts at negative displacement, not zero, and moves positive first. Particle X is at zero displacement at $t=0$ and must initially move in the negative direction.
